clue.text: Black, it fills void in minds

parts.note: B is the standard abbreviation for black, as on pencils

indicators.note: the word it goes into the gap of the void, filling it from inside

parts.note: a void is a bottomless pit or chasm, an abyss
taken as written

explanation.surface: Something dark seeping into empty heads, like a creeping sense of dread.
explanation.walkthrough: 'minds' looks like a noun for brains; it is the verb, as in minding the children.
explanation.definitionFit: To mind children is to look after them while their parents are out, the job of a sitter.

clue.text: Unusually big seat at theatre tipped up

parts.note: the bum is the seat you sit on

indicators.note: in a down entry, tipped up means the letters are turned to read upward

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre

explanation.surface: A theatre seat that tips up, unusually large for its occupant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tipped up' turns REP into PER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bumper crop or harvest is an exceptionally large one.

clue.text: What Hollywood does to preserve the King's discs, perhaps

indicators.note: preserving means keeping something safe inside, so the king's letter is enclosed

parts.note: Paul Hollywood is a British TV baker, a judge on The Great British Bake Off
R is for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A film studio protecting the King's records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to preserve' puts R inside BAKES. 'Hollywood' looks like the film industry; it is the baker.
explanation.definitionFit: Disc versions are one kind of vehicle stopping device, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Use plug, crudely inserting ruler and gum

indicators.note: the ruler letters are put into the rearranged letters
crudely means roughly made, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder, used letter for letter
fodder, used letter for letter
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A DIY bodge: jamming a plug in with a ruler and some gum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' looks like a measuring stick in this DIY scene; it is the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: Gum is glue, and this is a very strong, fast-setting adhesive.

clue.text: See 15
Functional black uniform goes on top

indicators.note: the uniform letter is placed first, ahead of the colour word

parts.note: U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
sable is the heraldic and poetic word for black

explanation.surface: A practical all-black outfit, with the uniform jacket worn over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes on top' places U ahead of SABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something functional can be put to use, so it is serviceable or fit for the job.

clue.text: Rod's beginning to suspect river personnel

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the Taff is a river in South Wales flowing through Cardiff

explanation.surface: A fishing rod's first hint that someone suspects the river staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod's' is a bonus definition too: a staff is a rod or stick.
explanation.definitionFit: The staff of an organisation are the people employed there.

clue.text: Advocates avoiding street obstacles

indicators.note: avoiding means leaving out, so the street letters are dropped

parts.note: barristers are lawyers who plead in court, advocates

explanation.surface: Lawyers dodging a street full of roadblocks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops ST from the lawyers' title.
explanation.definitionFit: Barriers are fences or blocks placed in the way, obstructions.

clue.text: Solver said record is English hymn

indicators.note: said signals a sound-alike: EU is pronounced like the word you, as in Eugene

parts.note: the solver is the person addressed, you
a log is a written record
taken as written

explanation.surface: A solver's remark about an English hymn being on record.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hymn' is a verb here, as in hymning someone's praises.
explanation.definitionFit: To hymn someone is to praise them highly in speech or writing.

clue.text: Bump into noisy old birds making pub grub

indicators.note: noisy signals that the word is to be heard rather than read, a sound-alike

parts.note: to bump into someone is to meet them by chance
pie is an old name for the magpie, so pies are old birds

explanation.surface: Coming across a flock of noisy old birds, perhaps around a pub table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'noisy' turns MEET into its sound-alike MEAT. Pie for magpie survives in the bird's full name.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastry pies filled with minced beef are classic cheap British pub food.

clue.text: Make the rounds every year to lake, crossing river

parts.note: PA stands for per annum, Latin for each year

indicators.note: the river letter lies across the path of the following words, so it sits within them

parts.note: taken as written
R is the map abbreviation for river
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A walker's annual hike down to the lake, crossing a river on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'every year' is the Latin per annum, the abbreviation familiar from salaries.
explanation.definitionFit: To patrol is to go round an area regularly, checking it as a guard or watchman does.

clue.text: Unnoticed 17 may be wasted by a magazine

definitions.text: Unnoticed 17 may be wasted by a magazine

parts.words: Unnoticed 17 may be wasted by a magazine
parts.note: 17 is an observer; an unseen watcher is a fly, which a rolled-up magazine might swat

explanation.surface: An unseen watcher who could be killed off by a magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 17-down is OBSERVER, which is also a newspaper, nodding at a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means an unseen witness, like a documentary maker observing quietly.

clue.text: Top man in Dubai backing agreement banks rejected

indicators.note: backing tells us to read the remaining letters in reverse order
the banks are the outer letters of agreement, two at each side, which are thrown away

explanation.surface: A Gulf ruler's deal falls through after the banks pull out.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping AG and NT from agreement leaves REEME, which 'backing' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: An emir, also spelt emeer, is a Muslim ruler; Dubai is ruled by one.

clue.text: Inspirational university place provided passion Henry's wanting

parts.note: PL is the abbreviation for place, as in street names
provided means if, on condition that

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so the letter for Henry is missing

parts.note: a passion is a thing, as in having a thing about someone
H is the symbol of the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A rousing campus where passion runs high, except for Henry, who lacks it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' removes H from THING, leaving TING.
explanation.definitionFit: Something uplifting raises the spirits, just as inspiring words or music do.

clue.text: Site manager in city's protecting wild flower king planted

indicators.note: the city's name wraps round the other letters, shielding them

parts.note: Cork is a city in the Republic of Ireland; the possessive gives the closing S

indicators.note: the king's letter is set down within the rearranged flower like a bulb
wild signals that the letters of flower are scrambled

parts.note: the fodder, used letter for letter
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A garden scene in an Irish city where a wild flower and a king have been planted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wild' scrambles the flower's letters before 'planted' sets the king among them; Cork is in the Republic of Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: This title belongs to the official who oversees building work on behalf of the client.

clue.text: Classic question concerning our security arrangements

definitions.text: Classic question concerning our security arrangements

parts.words: Classic question concerning our security arrangements
parts.note: Juvenal's Latin question Quis custodiet ipsos custodes; 'our' is the newspaper printing the puzzle

explanation.surface: An old riddle about who keeps watch over the people keeping us safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classic' means from the Classics: the Roman poet Juvenal. 'our' hints at the newspaper's own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Juvenal's line asks who keeps watch over the protectors themselves, a question of accountability.

clue.text: Harrison and Cartier's answer to last question?

definitions.text: Harrison and Cartier's answer to last question?

parts.words: Harrison and Cartier's answer to last question?
parts.note: John Harrison and Cartier made timepieces; the Latin line is often rendered as asking who watches over the watch-keepers

explanation.surface: Two famous names giving their reply to the previous question.
explanation.walkthrough: John Harrison was an 18th-century English clockmaker; Cartier makes luxury timepieces. 'last question' is 15/4.
explanation.definitionFit: Makers of timepieces could jokingly be called by this name, which also translates Juvenal's custodes.

clue.text: Network hub underpins heart of global paper

indicators.note: in a down entry the hub's letters sit beneath the central letters, supporting them
the heart of a word is its central letters

parts.note: a server is the central computer of a network

explanation.surface: A computer hub supporting the core of a worldwide newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: The Observer is a British Sunday newspaper, sister paper of the Guardian.
explanation.definitionFit: This title belongs to the oldest Sunday newspaper in Britain.

clue.text: Cutting books on the subject of getting into flying

indicators.note: the books and the subject word enter the flying word

parts.note: aviation is the business of flying aircraft
B is short for book, doubled for the plural as pp is for pages
RE is Latin for concerning, used for on the subject of

explanation.surface: Reading up on flying, perhaps by trimming the manuals down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting into' puts BBRE after the first A of AVIATION.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortening a word is cutting it down; the result is a short form like Dr.

clue.text: Nanny state dumps rubbish, cutting loss

indicators.note: the shortened state word cuts into the loss word

parts.note: a cost is something lost or sacrificed

indicators.note: dumps means throws out, so the rubbish letters leave the state word

parts.note: tat is cheap rubbish, junk

explanation.surface: A nanny state cuts its losses by dumping rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nanny state' reads as a phrase; the first word alone is the definition, used as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To nanny someone is to pamper or overprotect them, much as one would coddle a child.

clue.text: It's paid for in agreement with daughter

parts.note: to be at one is to agree

explanation.surface: A father settling up, in harmony with his daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paid for' means made amends for, as a sin is.
explanation.definitionFit: Making amends for a wrong is paying for it morally, as with a sin.

clue.text: Clubs find out about a church blessing

parts.note: C is the card-game abbreviation for clubs

indicators.note: about means around, so the learning word goes round the A

parts.note: to find out is to learn something
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Golfers or a society discovering a church's blessing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts A inside LEARN, making LEARAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Official permission or approval, a go-ahead, is the sense in which a blessing is given.

clue.text: Magistrate constantly rose to defend earl

indicators.note: the turned letters surround the earl letter to guard it
in a down entry, rose means the letters climb upward and so read backwards

parts.note: ever means always, constantly

explanation.surface: A magistrate who always stood up to defend an earl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rose' turns EVER into REVE; 'to defend' puts E inside, after R.
explanation.definitionFit: A reeve was a local official in medieval England with judicial duties.

clue.text: What secures runner's autograph?

definitions.meaning: a fastener: a bolt bent into a horseshoe shape and threaded at both ends
the sprinter Usain Bolt might sign himself with initial and surname

explanation.surface: A fan wondering how to get hold of an athlete's signature.
explanation.walkthrough: Usain Bolt is the Jamaican sprinter, so his signature reads U plus his surname.
explanation.definitionFit: This fixing is used to clamp pipes or exhausts, holding them fast.

clue.text: Films script involving old battle

indicators.note: involving means enclosing, so the script letters wrap the rest

parts.note: MS is short for manuscript, a handwritten script
to vie is to compete or battle

explanation.surface: A screenplay about an ancient battle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involving' puts OVIE inside MS.
explanation.definitionFit: Films are what Americans call the pictures shown in a cinema.

clue.text: Guitarist set aside hour for troops

indicators.note: set aside means removed, so the hour letter is dropped

parts.note: George Harrison, lead guitarist of the Beatles, written with his initial

explanation.surface: A guitarist cancels an hour's rehearsal to play for the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping the H of his surname from G. Harrison leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A body of soldiers stationed in a town or fort to defend it.

clue.text: Former railwaymen's assets regularly omitted tenders

parts.note: the NUR, the National Union of Railwaymen, was a British trade union, since merged

indicators.note: every other letter of assets is dropped, keeping the alternate ones

explanation.surface: A union's assets being left out of tenders for a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly omitted' takes alternate letters of assets, keeping S, E, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Those who tend the sick are carers in hospitals, a playful sense of tenders.

clue.text: Key Latin dictionary ready to be loaded in camera

parts.note: C is a musical key

indicators.note: the ready word is packed into the dictionary letters like a cargo

parts.note: OED is the Oxford English Dictionary
set means prepared or ready

explanation.surface: Packing a Latin dictionary into a camera bag, ready for a trip.
explanation.walkthrough: In camera is a legal phrase for in private, so 'camera' here has nothing to do with photography.
explanation.definitionFit: Shut away in private discussion, as in a meeting held behind closed doors.
